evidence.observation: Declares the settings layering primitive with the comment "Deep merge settings: project/overrides take precedence, nested objects merge recursively". It delegates to deepMergeObjects (169-186), which skips undefined override values and recursively merges plain objects, so a nested project override (e.g. retry.maxRetries) wins without discarding sibling user keys.

The private constructor stores globalSettings (user scope) and projectSettings separately, then sets this.settings = deepMergeSettings(this.globalSettings, this.projectSettings) at line 350. This line is where the user-vs-project precedence is fixed: project values override user values, and the merged result is what every getter reads.

Maps the two settings scopes to concrete files: the global (user) scope is <agentDir>/settings.json and the project scope is <cwd>/settings.json under CONFIG_DIR_NAME (= ".pi"), i.e. <cwd>/.pi/settings.json.

Returns {} for the project scope when projectTrusted is false (lines 411-413), and tryLoadFromStorage turns parse failures into {} plus an error. An untrusted project's .pi/settings.json therefore contributes nothing and the merge falls back to user settings and defaults.

Documented as "Apply additional overrides on top of current settings" and implemented as deepMergeSettings(this.settings, overrides). Because this.settings already merges user+project, this method is the layer above project settings (used by the CLI). Overrides affect only this.settings; save() recomputes this.settings from the two file scopes, so CLI overrides are runtime-only and are not persisted.

Reads this.globalSettings.cacheWarming directly (comment: "Read from global settings only because warming costs money") and falls back to "streaming". This is a user/global-only setting with no project layer, in contrast with getters such as getTransport that read the merged this.settings.

Reads this.globalSettings.defaultProjectTrust and coerces any value other than "always"/"never" to "ask". Another explicit global-only setting, consistent with the Settings interface comment "default: ask; global setting only" at line 128.

Demonstrates the built-in default layer beneath both file scopes: each field is this.settings.retry?.field ?? <constant> (maxRetries 3, baseDelayMs 2000, maxAgentDelayMs DEFAULT_MAX_AGENT_RETRY_DELAY_MS). The default applies only when neither user nor project supplied the value.

Public entry point for resolving a config string. parseConfigValueReference decides the kind; a leading "!" executes the remainder as a shell command via executeCommand (cached per process), otherwise the parsed template interpolates $VAR/${VAR} and returns the literal result. The doc comment (138-144) states the order: shell command, then env interpolation, then literal.

First decision in the value-resolution precedence: config.startsWith("!") produces { type: "command" }; every other string becomes { type: "template", parts } via parseConfigValueTemplate, which recognizes $NAME, ${NAME}, $$ and $! escapes.

Second-level precedence inside a template: an explicitly supplied env record (env?.[name]) wins over process.env[name], then undefined. Returning undefined makes resolveTemplate (101-113) abort and the whole template resolve to undefined.

Applies the same resolveConfigValue logic to every header value and drops entries that resolve falsy. Confirms this module is the shared credential/value-resolution layer (used by auth-storage and model-registry) rather than a settings-scope merger.

The CLI wiring for the top settings layer: when interactive and --use-theme was passed, main.ts calls startupSettingsManager.applyOverrides({ theme: parsed.useTheme }). Nearby, sessionDir is resolved at 676-679 as --session-dir > environment session dir > settings.getSessionDir().

Documents and implements a parallel precedence for model selection: 1. CLI args (provider + model) at line 648, 2. first scoped/enabled model, 3. restored session, 4. saved default from settings, 5. first available model. CLI again outranks the persisted settings default.

claims.claim: The effective settings precedence is CLI overrides > project settings (<cwd>/.pi/settings.json) > user/global settings (<agentDir>/settings.json) > built-in defaults.

Project settings override user settings, including nested keys, because the SettingsManager constructor merges with deepMergeSettings(globalSettings, projectSettings) and deepMergeObjects recurses into plain objects while ignoring undefined overrides.

The project layer is conditional on project trust: loadFromStorage returns {} for the project scope when projectTrusted is false, and setProjectTrusted(false) clears projectSettings and recomputes the merge, so an untrusted repository's .pi/settings.json cannot outrank user settings.

CLI values are applied above the merged user+project settings: main.ts calls applyOverrides for --use-theme, --session-dir resolves as CLI > environment > settings, and findInitialModel gives CLI provider/model priority 1 over the saved settings default.

Some settings are intentionally global-only and therefore have no project or merge-level override: getCacheWarmingMode and getDefaultProjectTrust read this.globalSettings, matching the interface comment "global setting only".

Built-in defaults are the lowest layer and are applied per getter after the scope merge, e.g. getRetrySettings uses this.settings.retry?.field ?? <constant>, so a value present in either user or project scope suppresses the default.

resolve-config-value.ts defines a separate value-resolution precedence for credential/config strings: a leading "!" means execute the remainder as a shell command; otherwise the string is a template where an explicitly supplied env map outranks process.env, literals resolve to themselves, and an unresolved env var makes the whole value undefined.

conclusion:
Precedence table for packages/coding-agent/src/core settings (highest wins).

| Rank | Layer | Storage / source | How it is applied | Evidence symbols |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | CLI flags | Process argv (parseArgs) | applyOverrides() deep-merges onto the already-merged settings (theme); --session-dir resolves CLI > env > settings; findInitialModel gives CLI provider/model priority 1 | settings-manager.ts:567-570 (applyOverrides), main.ts:666-668, model-resolver.ts:622-649 (findInitialModel) |
| 2 | Project settings | <cwd>/.pi/settings.json (CONFIG_DIR_NAME) | deepMergeSettings(globalSettings, projectSettings) in the constructor; only loaded when the project is trusted | settings-manager.ts:332-351, 234-239 (FileSettingsStorage.constructor), 410-426 (loadFromStorage) |
| 3 | User / global settings | <agentDir>/settings.json | Base of the merge; also the sole source for global-only settings | settings-manager.ts:234-239, 350, 954-958 (getCacheWarmingMode), 1031-1034 (getDefaultProjectTrust) |
| 4 | Built-in defaults | Constants / per-getter ?? fallbacks | Applied after the merge when neither scope defines the field | settings-manager.ts:188-191 (deepMergeSettings), 932-939 (getRetrySettings), 18-21 (DEFAULT_COMPACTION_TOKEN_SETTINGS) |

Notes:
- Nested objects merge recursively (deepMergeObjects, settings-manager.ts:169-186), so project settings can override individual nested keys (e.g. retry.maxRetries) without discarding sibling user keys.
- The project layer is gated by trust: an untrusted project contributes {} (settings-manager.ts:411-413), so its settings fall through to user settings and defaults.
- CLI overrides applied via applyOverrides are runtime-only: save() recomputes this.settings from the two file scopes (settings-manager.ts:669), so they are never persisted.
- A parallel CLI-first precedence exists for model/credential selection: findInitialModel ranks CLI args above saved settings defaults, and resolve-config-value.ts independently ranks "!command" > $ENV template (explicit env over process.env) > literal for credential/header values.
